newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco chooses Chase Manhattan to lead big loan.
newsitem.headline: Codelco chooses Chase Manhattan to lead big loan.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Bank will act as principal agent in a $500 million, five-year syndicated loan for Corporacion Nacional del Cobre de Chile, or Codelco, the state copper company said.
The loan, announced earlier by Codelco CEO Juan Villarzu, will carry an interest rate of 0.225 percent over Libor with a single repayment after five years, it said in a statement.
"These are the best conditions ever obtained by a Chilean company," Villarzu said in a speech at an investment seminar.
He said the loan would go toward financing the company's $3.3 billion "investment plan" to the end of the decade, which includes building the Radomiro Tomic mine and expansion at the Andina mine.
The rest of the financing for the loan will come from internal sources and the sale of assets, he said.

Codelco, formed in the early 1970s when Chile nationalized several U.S.-owned copper mines, has long sought large-scale foreign financing for its expansion plans. The company said last week it received offers from 11 banks to act as principal agent.
Though it remains the world's largest copper producer, Codelco's share of total Chilean production of the metal has shrunk to just under half as private mining investment has risen.
